title: The Handover Note That Saved Monday
script: Narrator: [warmly] Before taking three days of leave, I believed my team knew everything about my tasks. We sat in the same room and spoke every day.
Narrator: On my final afternoon, my manager asked for a short handover note. I nearly wrote only, “Please check my email if needed.”
Narrator: [honestly] Then I imagined my coworker opening hundreds of messages while a customer waited. I made a clearer page.
Narrator: For each active task, I wrote its current position, next action, deadline, and the person to contact.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I included links to shared files, but I did not copy passwords or private customer data into the note.
Narrator: I marked one task as urgent because a supplier needed an answer on Monday morning. Two other tasks could wait until I returned.
Narrator: [carefully] Before leaving, I spent ten minutes with Laila, the coworker covering my work. She asked about one unclear deadline.
Narrator: Her question helped me find an error. I had written Tuesday, but the supplier's email clearly said Monday.
Narrator: [reflective] During my leave, nobody called me. At first, I worried this meant something had gone wrong.
Narrator: When I returned, Laila showed me the completed supplier task. The handover had given her enough information and authority to act.
Narrator: [practically] She also added two notes about decisions she made. I could continue the work without asking her to remember every detail.
Narrator: The process taught me that a handover is not a list of everything I know. It is a path for the next person.
Narrator: [calmly] Clear priorities matter because every task cannot be urgent. Safe shared access matters because useful links should not expose secrets.
Narrator: Now I update a small handover page each Friday, even when no leave is planned.
Narrator: [encouraging] The note takes a few minutes, but it protects customers, coworkers, and my own rest when I am away.

quiz.question: Why did the manager request a note?
options: The narrator was taking three days of leave
quiz.explanation: The note would cover work during a short absence.

quiz.question: What did each task entry include?
options: Status, next action, deadline, and contact

quiz.question: What information was kept out?
quiz.explanation: Security was part of the handover.

quiz.question: What error did Laila catch?
options: A Monday deadline was written as Tuesday
quiz.explanation: A quick discussion corrected the urgent date.

quiz.question: How does the narrator describe a handover?
options: A path for the next person
A list where all tasks are urgent
quiz.explanation: The best note helps another person act safely.

quiz.question: Why was conversation alone insufficient?
options: Details could be forgotten while the narrator was away
quiz.explanation: A shared room did not guarantee shared knowledge.

quiz.question: What did every task entry identify?
options: Status, deadline, next action, and contact
quiz.explanation: The note focused on needed operational facts.

quiz.question: Why exclude sensitive information?
options: The handover should not expose private data
quiz.explanation: Useful sharing still follows data boundaries.

quiz.question: How did the note protect rest?
options: Coworkers could act without contacting the person on leave
